answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust grow only from time and verified work. Each identity earns standing by completing attested tasks for peers, and it strengthens slowly, like dawn light: a fresh account may transact, but only in tiny amounts, rate-limited. Reputation cannot be bought or forged. An attacker who spins up a gale of fake identities gains nothing — each starts at zero, and reaching real limits takes weeks of costly work per identity, while one fraud wipes that history. Honest newcomers still get in — the velvet glove — but scale without history buys no influence.
